events.title: Scala first public release
events.summary: Martin Odersky announced the first Scala implementation on the JVM on January 20, 2004 at EPFL.
events.about: Scala merges object-oriented and functional programming on the JVM — case classes, pattern matching, implicits, and seamless Java interop. It powers Apache Spark (big data), Akka (actors), and Twitter's early backend. Kotlin and Swift borrowed ideas from Scala's type system and syntax.

narrative.whyChosen: Scala showed the JVM could host modern FP+OO languages beyond Java without a new runtime.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the language of big-data (Spark) and proved functional features could scale to industry codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: Java lacked expressive abstraction for components; researchers needed a scalable language for composable software.
